keywords.def: finally, after a series of event
(to do something) annoying or difficult (to do something)
(with an ingredient) use too much (of an ingredient)

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《6分钟英语》。

sentences.en: I'm Pippa. And I'm Georgie. In this programme, we're talking about saving money on food.
sentences.zh: 我是Pippa。我是Georgie。在这一期节目中，我们将讨论如何在购买食物上省钱。

sentences.en: Pippa, are you good at saving money on your food shop?
sentences.zh: Pippa，你很擅长在买菜时省钱吗？

sentences.en: I think I'm quite good. I plan what I like to cook so I don't waste money in the supermarket.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我挺擅长的。我会计划好自己想做哪些菜，这样就不会在超市里浪费钱了。

sentences.en: How about you, Georgie? I'm not very good.
sentences.zh: 你呢，Georgie？我不太擅长。

sentences.en: I usually go to the supermarket when I'm hungry, so I end up buying lots of snacks.
sentences.zh: 我通常饿着肚子去超市，结果买了一大堆零食。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a terrible idea. Well, in this programme we'll be learning about one way to save money on the food we eat.
sentences.zh: 哦，那可真是个糟糕的主意。嗯，在这期节目中，我们将了解一种在我们所吃的食物上省钱的方法。

sentences.en: But first, I've got a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 但首先，我有一个问题要问你，Georgie。

sentences.en: The most expensive restaurant in the world is thought to be a restaurant called Sublimotion in Ibiza, which only has 12 customers each night.
sentences.zh: 世界上最贵的餐厅据说是位于伊比沙岛的Sublimotion餐厅，它每晚只接待12位顾客。

sentences.en: But how much in euros is a meal per person at the restaurant?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这个餐厅里，每人吃一顿饭要多少欧元？

sentences.en: a) €650 b) €1,650 c) €2,650 The most expensive… I'll go with c) €2,650.
sentences.zh: a) 650欧元 b) 1,650欧元 c) 2,650欧元 最贵的……我选c) 2,650欧元。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Now, food in the UK is getting more expensive, as it has been in many parts of the world, and some people are struggling to afford their food shopping.
sentences.zh: 现在，英国的食品价格越来越贵，就像世界上许多地方一样，有些人甚至难以负担买菜的开销。

sentences.en: But BBC World Service programme, People Fixing the World, has been finding out about a project called ‘ Bags of Taste’ which helps people save money on their food shopping and improve their diet at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但BBC世界频道的节目《People Fixing the World》一直在了解一个名为“Bags of Taste”的项目，它帮助人们在买菜时省钱，同时改善他们的饮食。

sentences.en: Bags of something is an informal way to say a lot of something.
sentences.zh: “Bags of something”是“很多某物”的非正式说法。

sentences.en: The founder of Bags of Taste, Alicia Weston, became concerned that people in the UK with less money found it difficult to afford a healthy diet People in poverty are eating the worst diets and they are getting sicker younger.
sentences.zh: “Bags of Taste”的创始人Alicia Weston开始担心，英国收入较少的人很难负担得起健康的饮食。贫困人口的饮食最差，而且他们生病时更年轻。

sentences.en: And we know that diets are the single largest cause of health inequalities in the UK.
sentences.zh: 而且我们知道，饮食是英国健康不平等的最单一最大成因。

sentences.en: Alicia found that people didn't know how to cook the kinds of meals they'd like to eat, and they couldn't afford to experiment.
sentences.zh: Alicia发现，人们不知道如何烹饪他们想吃的那类饭菜，而且他们也负担不起尝试的成本。

sentences.en: Imagine spending lots of money on ingredients and then wasting them by cooking them badly or burning the food.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，花了很多钱买食材，然后因为厨艺不佳或把食物烧焦而浪费了它们。

sentences.en: People also thought making healthy food would be too expensive and take too much time.
sentences.zh: 人们还认为制作健康食品会太昂贵，而且花费太多时间。

sentences.en: So ultimately, we've been able to come up with a programme that basically can tackle all of these issues.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，我们能够推出一个基本上能解决所有这些问题的项目。

sentences.en: So what we do now is we deliver all of the ingredients to their door, because ultimately, behaviour change starts with actually changing your behaviour at home.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在做的是，把所有的食材直接送到他们家门口，因为归根结底，行为改变始于你在家里真正改变自己的行为。

sentences.en: Alicia says that ultimately,she'sbeen able to come up with a solution to help people save money on healthy food.
sentences.zh: Alicia说，最终，她能够想出一个解决方案来帮助人们在健康食品上省钱。

sentences.en: We can use the adverb ultimately to mean finally, after a series of events have happened.
sentences.zh: 我们可以使用副词“ultimately”来表示“最终”，即经过一系列事件之后发生的事情。

sentences.en: Alicia wants to tackle the things that stop people eating healthy food on a budget.
sentences.zh: Alicia想要解决那些阻碍人们在预算有限的情况下吃上健康食品的问题。

sentences.en: If you tackle a problem, you try to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 如果你“tackle”一个问题，你就是在试着去处理它、应对它。

sentences.en: Alicia's solution involves delivering ingredients and recipes to people and then using a WhatsApp group to talk to participants.
sentences.zh: Alicia的解决方案包括将食材和食谱送到人们手中，然后通过WhatsApp群组与参与者交流。

sentences.en: Each WhatsApp group has a mentor who shares cooking tips and advice.
sentences.zh: 每个WhatsApp群组都有一个导师，负责分享烹饪小贴士和建议。

sentences.en: To give you an idea of how this works, the team at People Fixing the World read out some of the messages on one of the ' Bags of Taste' WhatsApp chats Amy, mentor Remember to put the fridge bag in the fridge.
sentences.zh: 为了让你了解这是如何运作的，《People Fixing the World》团队宣读了其中一个“Bags of Taste”WhatsApp聊天群里的一些消息。导师Amy：记得把冰箱里的袋子放进冰箱。

sentences.en: Can we aim to cook recipe one by Tuesday evening?
sentences.zh: 我们的目标能定在星期二晚上之前做好第一道菜吗？

sentences.en: Our first recipe, chana masala is a classic.
sentences.zh: 我们的第一道菜，鹰嘴豆咖喱（chana masala），是一道经典之作。

sentences.en: It needs an onion, which can be a pain to chop.
sentences.zh: 它需要一个洋葱，切洋葱可能会很让人头疼。

sentences.en: So, try our way. [video posted] Love this method [chef emoji].
sentences.zh: 所以，试试我们的方法吧。［发布了视频］太喜欢这个方法了［厨师表情符号］。

sentences.en: First time I've chopped an onion like this and it's so neat and easy.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次这样切洋葱，既整齐又简单。

sentences.en: I'm going to cook mine tomorrow. Looking forward to it.
sentences.zh: 我明天就要做我的那份了。非常期待。

sentences.en: I've finished making my chana masala. I was a bit too heavy-handed with the chilli.
sentences.zh: 我做完鹰嘴豆咖喱了。我的辣椒好像下得有点儿太重了。

sentences.en: My husband likes a lot of spice. So, I'd reduce that next time.
sentences.zh: 我丈夫喜欢吃很辣的。所以，下次我会少放一点。

sentences.en: The mentor in the group, Amy, describes the recipe for chana masala as a classic.
sentences.zh: 群里的导师Amy将鹰嘴豆咖喱的食谱描述为经典之作（classic）。

sentences.en: We call something a classic to say that it is well-known and of good quality.
sentences.zh: 我们把某物称为经典，是为了说明它广为人知且品质优良。

sentences.en: We can also describe a particular book, film or song as a classic.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以把某本特定的书、某部电影或某首歌描述为经典。

sentences.en: Amy sends a video to show a technique for cutting onions, which she describes as a pain tochop.
sentences.zh: Amy发了一个视频来展示切洋葱的技巧，她形容切洋葱“a pain to chop”（令人头疼）。

sentences.en: If something is a pain to do, it is difficult or annoying to do.
sentences.zh: 如果做某事是“a pain to do”，那就是说做这件事很困难或很烦人。

sentences.en: One of the participants, Ally, said that when she made the chana masala, she was a bit heavy-handed with the chilli.
sentences.zh: 其中一位参与者Ally说，她在做鹰嘴豆咖喱时，辣椒放得有点儿太重了（heavy-handed）。

sentences.en: If you are heavy-handed with an ingredient, you use too much of it, and so Ally's chana masala was very spicy!
sentences.zh: 如果你对某种食材“heavy-handed”，意思就是你用得太多了，所以Ally的鹰嘴豆咖喱非常辣！

sentences.en: Bags of Taste helps people learn new recipes and cook healthy food without spending too much money.
sentences.zh: “Bags of Taste”帮助人们学习新的食谱并烹饪健康的食物，而不需要花太多钱。

sentences.en: It's certainly a lot cheaper than a meal at the restaurant in my question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 这肯定比我问题里那家餐厅的一顿饭便宜多了，Georgie。

sentences.en: I asked you how much it costs for a meal at Sublimotion, thought to be the most expensive restaurant in the world.
sentences.zh: 我问过你，在被认为是世界上最贵的Sublimotion餐厅吃一顿饭要花多少钱。

sentences.en: Yes, I said a meal was €2,650. Well, you were wrong.
sentences.zh: 对，我说一顿饭要2,650欧元。嗯，你猜错了。

sentences.en: It's actually €1,650, but I think that's still pretty expensive.
sentences.zh: 实际上是1,650欧元，但我认为那依然相当贵。

sentences.en: It definitely is. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with bags of, which means a lot of something.
sentences.zh: 确实很贵。好了。让我们回顾一下所学词汇，首先是“bags of”，意思是很多某物。

sentences.en: We can use the adverb ultimately to say finally, after a series of events.
sentences.zh: 我们可以使用副词“ultimately”来表示“最终”，即在一系列事件发生之后。

sentences.en: If you tackle a problem, you try to deal with it and find a solution If we describe something, like a recipe, as a classic, we mean it's well-known and of good quality.
sentences.zh: 如果你“tackle”一个问题，你就是在试着去处理它并找到解决方案。如果我们把某样东西（比如食谱）描述为“classic”，意思是它广为人知且品质优良。

sentences.en: If something is a pain to do, it is annoying or difficult to do.
sentences.zh: 如果做某事是“a pain to do”，那就是说这件事很烦人或很困难。

sentences.en: And if you are heavy-handed with an ingredient, you use too much of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某种食材“heavy-handed”，意思就是你用得太多了。

sentences.en: For example, I made some soup the other day and I was a bit heavy-handed with the salt – it tasted disgusting!
sentences.zh: 例如，我前几天做了一些汤，结果盐放得有点重——尝起来太难以下咽了！

sentences.en: Oh, that's not very good! OK, once again, our 6 minutes are up.
sentences.zh: 哦，那可真不太妙！好了，我们的6分钟又到了。

sentences.en: But you can test what you've learned with the interactive quiz on our website.
sentences.zh: 但你可以通过我们网站上的互动小测验来检验你学到了什么。

sentences.en: Visit bbclearningenglish.com. Bye for now.
sentences.zh: 访问bbclearningenglish.com。一会儿见。

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
